subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage:
Monday. In the school corridor, Ramesh's friend Jatin went pale when he saw the notice board with the results. Ramesh laughed and said, "Scared?" Jatin's lips were tight and he said nothing.

Wednesday. During assembly in the hot sun, Jatin's face went white again, he swayed and his hands felt cold. Ramesh held his arm and said, "Sit down." A teacher brought water and asked him to rest.

Friday. Jatin's mother took him to the doctor. He was fine, just skipping breakfast. He told Ramesh, "Monday was fear, Wednesday was the sun and no food." Ramesh nodded. "Now I know to ask."

qa.q: What did Ramesh do when Jatin swayed at assembly?
qa.a: He held Jatin's arm and told him to sit down.

qa.q: What could Jatin's pale face on Monday and Wednesday have meant, and how did they turn out?
qa.a: Monday's paleness came from fear about the results, while Wednesday's came from the hot sun and no breakfast. The same look had two different causes.

qa.q: What should someone do when a friend goes pale and dizzy?
qa.a: Help them sit down, get water and call an adult, as Ramesh and the teacher did.

qa.q: How might Ramesh have felt when he said "Scared?" and later saw Jatin sway?
qa.a: He may have felt guilty for joking and worried when Jatin swayed. His "Now I know to ask" suggests he learned to check first.

grounding: A child who goes pale may be scared, ill or faint, and sudden paleness with dizziness needs sitting down, water and adult help.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Pallavi, listen. When I was your age, at my school near Kochi, my friend Himani went pale in the middle of the test. I thought she'd seen a ghost. Her lips were grey and she was blinking slowly. "Are you scared?" I whispered. She said, "I feel strange." I put my hand up and called the teacher. The teacher sat Himani down and gave her water, and they took her to the nurse. It turned out she had skipped breakfast and the room was very stuffy. I've never forgotten that day. From it I learnt that a pale face has many stories and the first thing to do is sit the person down and get an adult.

qa.q: What did Himani say when asked if she was scared?
qa.a: She said, "I feel strange."

qa.q: What did Himani's pale face and slow blinking suggest, and what did it turn out to be?
qa.a: It suggested she might be scared or unwell, and it turned out she skipped breakfast in a stuffy room. The face alone could not tell the cause.

qa.q: What could a student do if a classmate goes pale in the middle of a test?
qa.a: Tell the teacher straight away, as the narrator did, and help the classmate sit down and get water.

qa.q: How might Himani have felt as the teacher and nurse helped her?
qa.a: She said she felt strange, so she was probably unsure and unsteady, and likely relieved to have adults help.

grounding: An elder recalls a classmate who went pale for reasons other than fear, and the need to sit down, drink water and involve an adult.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage:
On the school trip bus to the dam, it was hot and crowded, and the road wound up and down the hills. Halfway, Trisha went very pale. She clutched the seat in front.
Jagdish Sir noticed from the aisle. Was she scared of the steep drop outside the window? Feeling sick? Cold from the air conditioning?
He made his way to her. "Trisha, are you dizzy?"
She nodded, eyes closed.
He helped her sit lower, gave her his water bottle, and asked the driver to stop at the next lay-by. Outside in the shade, she sipped slowly. Colour came back into her cheeks.
"I didn't eat breakfast," she whispered.
Sir called her mother to let her know and kept her in the front seat for the rest of the trip.

qa.q: What did Jagdish Sir give Trisha?
qa.a: His water bottle.

qa.q: What was Jagdish Sir thinking when he saw Trisha go pale?
qa.a: He felt concerned and was unsure of the cause, wondering whether she was scared, feeling sick, or cold.

qa.q: What did Jagdish Sir do that was right for a pale, dizzy child?
qa.a: He had her sit, gave water, stopped the bus, and called her mother, which is the right response for sudden paleness with dizziness.

qa.q: How might Trisha have felt when the bus stopped?
qa.a: Trisha probably felt relieved and a little embarrassed to be the reason for the stop.

grounding: On a hot winding bus, a child goes pale for an uncertain reason, and a teacher has her sit, drink water and tells her parent.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage:
On a foggy December morning at the bus stop in Delhi, Himani noticed her little brother Siddharth's face had gone white.
"Scared of the maths test?" she teased.
He didn't answer. His lips were pale, and he swayed slightly.
Himani's teasing stopped. "Siddharth? Are you dizzy?"
"A bit," he mumbled. "And cold."
She made him sit on the bench, wrapped her own scarf round his neck, and gave him water from her bottle. Then she called Mummy. "Siddharth's gone pale and dizzy at the bus stop."
Mummy came running down in her slippers. They skipped the bus, and Mummy took him back home to rest and warm up.

qa.q: What did Himani wrap round Siddharth's neck?
qa.a: Her own scarf.

qa.q: What was Himani feeling when her teasing stopped?
qa.a: She felt worried and alarmed, realising Siddharth might be dizzy or unwell, not just scared of the test.

qa.q: What steps did Himani take that were right?
qa.a: She had him sit, gave him water and her scarf, and called Mummy for adult help.

qa.q: How might Siddharth have felt when Mummy came running?
qa.a: He probably felt relieved and safe that an adult was there to help.

grounding: A child's paleness could mean fear or cold, and an older sibling has him sit, gives water and gets adult help.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage:
"Arohi, you've gone white!"
"I'm fine, Ankita. It's just... his knee."
They both looked at Mithun's scraped knee, bleeding onto his sock.
"You look like you'll faint."
"I feel wobbly."
"Sit down. Right here, on the step."
Arohi sat. Ankita held out her water bottle. "Drink."
"I hate blood," Arohi whispered.
"I know. Don't look at it. Look at me."
Ankita waved at the teacher on duty. "Ma'am! Arohi's pale and dizzy, and Mithun's knee is bleeding!"
The teacher came fast, took Mithun to the first-aid room, and sat with Arohi till her colour came back.

qa.q: Whose knee was bleeding?
qa.a: Mithun's.

qa.q: What was Arohi feeling when she went pale?
qa.a: Arohi felt shocked and faint at the sight of blood, and wobbly.

qa.q: What did Ankita do that was wise?
qa.a: She had Arohi sit, gave her water, helped her look away, and called the teacher for adult help.

qa.q: How might the teacher on duty have seen the situation?
qa.a: The teacher saw two children needing help and acted quickly, caring for both Mithun and Arohi.

grounding: A child goes pale from shock at blood, and a friend has her sit, gives water, and calls an adult.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: I'm Lokesh, and last month I was meant to read the thought for the day in assembly. We had been standing in the sun for ages. When I walked to the mike, my ears started buzzing and the ground felt tilted. Sangeeta, who was next in line, whispered, "You've gone white! Are you that scared?" I didn't know. Maybe I was scared. Maybe it was the sun, or that I had skipped breakfast. Mr Menon saw my face and didn't wait to find out. He sat me down on the steps in the shade, gave me water and sent Sangeeta running for the school nurse. The nurse checked me and called home. Sangeeta read the thought for the day instead. I read it the next week.

qa.q: What was Lokesh meant to read in assembly?
qa.a: The thought for the day.

qa.q: What was Lokesh feeling when Sangeeta asked about being scared?
qa.a: Lokesh felt dizzy and confused, and honestly unsure whether the paleness came from fear, the sun or a skipped breakfast.

qa.q: Why was Mr Menon right not to wait to find out the cause?
qa.a: Sudden paleness with buzzing ears and a tilting feeling needs sitting down, water and adult help whatever the cause, so he acted and sent for the nurse.

qa.q: How did Sangeeta read Lokesh's white face?
qa.a: Sangeeta took it as stage fright, one possible reading, when heat or hunger might have caused it too.

grounding: It illustrates that a child going pale may be scared, overheated or unwell, and that paleness with dizziness calls for sitting down, water and adult help.
